item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00392","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C21","C22","C25"],"selected_candidate_label":"C21","confidence":0.83,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C21 plausibly supplied the principal structural template for the child: creation of a presidential commission, assignment to survey a federal personnel-benefit system and formulate recommendations, enumeration of substantive considerations, mandatory agency cooperation, administrative support provisions, and a final report due on the identical calendar date of November 1. C22 is also a strong possible source for narrower features—five-member presidential body, Civil Service Commission support, career-service eligibility, and criteria introduced by a 'guided' clause—but it does not match the child's temporary study-and-report architecture as closely. C25 has substantially similar commission machinery but fewer distinctive correspondences than C21.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The Committee shall develop specific recommendations with respect to the establishment of a Career Executive Program within the civil-service system.","parent_excerpt":"The Commission is authorized and directed to make a comprehensive survey and appraisal of the structure, scope, and administration of the laws ... and it shall make recommendations to the President regarding policies which ... should guide the granting of such benefits in the future.","explanation":"Both establish a temporary presidential body to examine an existing federal administrative system and formulate policy recommendations for its future structure."},{"child_excerpt":"The objectives of the Career Executive Program recommended by the Committee shall be ... [followed by enumerated considerations].","parent_excerpt":"The Commission shall give particular attention to: [followed by three enumerated considerations].","explanation":"The child adapts C21's sequence of a broad study-and-recommendation mandate followed by a separate enumerated list directing the body's substantive analysis."},{"child_excerpt":"Subject to law, the heads of departments and agencies shall cooperate with and assist the Committee in carrying out the provisions of this order.","parent_excerpt":"All executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government are authorized and directed to cooperate with the Commission in its work and to furnish the Commission such information and assistance, not inconsistent with law, as it may require in the performance of its functions.","explanation":"The cooperation provision closely condenses the same legal and administrative mechanism."},{"child_excerpt":"The Committee shall report to the President not later than November 1, 1957","parent_excerpt":"The Commission shall make a final written report, including findings and recommendations, to the President ... not later than November 1, 1955.","explanation":"The identical November 1 deadline, coupled with the same recommendation-producing commission structure, is a concrete textual correspondence beyond generic reporting boilerplate."}]}
